title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a short, self-contained topological computation written on the back of recycled administrative paper (c. 1975). It is apparently unrelated to the Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs material of the folder.

Setting (inferred):
- X is a locally compact space, e.g. a manifold or the underlying space of a variety, 'tame at infinity'.
- X̂ = X ∪ {ω} is its Alexandroff one-point compactification.
- T is a closed contractible conic neighbourhood of ω in X̂, with interior T° and frontier ∂T = S_ω, the 'link at infinity'.
- X' = X̂ − T° is compact; it is X with an end-collar removed.

The classes C_∞ and E_X are not defined on this page. The most plausible reading is that E_X is the class of spaces homotopy equivalent to X (or admissible models of X), and C_∞ is some class of nice compact spaces such as compact C^∞ manifolds with boundary. Grothendieck verifies:
- (a) X' ∈ C_∞, hence X' ∈ E_X;
- (b) X' is homotopy equivalent to X = X̂ − ω, hence X ∈ E_{X'}.
In short, X' is a compact model of the homotopy type of X.

NB computation:
- Mayer–Vietoris for X̂ = X' ∪ T with X' ∩ T = ∂T gives χ(X) = χ(X') = χ(X̂) − χ(T) + χ(∂T).
- T is contractible, so χ(T) = 1.
- χ(X̂) − 1 = χ_!(X), the compactly supported Euler characteristic.
- Hence χ(X) − χ_!(X) = χ(S_ω). The defect between ordinary and compactly supported Euler characteristic is the Euler characteristic of the link at infinity, i.e. it 'expresses the local structure of X at infinity'.

Remarks:
- For an n-manifold, Poincaré duality gives χ_! = (−1)^n χ, so χ(S_ω) = (1 − (−1)^n) χ(X).
- For a complex variety the link at infinity is an odd-dimensional manifold when smooth, so χ(S_ω) = 0 and χ = χ_c. This is consistent with the known equality χ = χ_c for complex algebraic varieties.
errors: The argument tacitly needs X̂ to admit a contractible (conic) closed neighbourhood T of ω with a collar, so that X' ⊂ X is a deformation retract and Mayer–Vietoris applies. This holds for tame spaces (algebraic or semi-algebraic, triangulable compactification) but not for arbitrary locally compact spaces. The page does not state these hypotheses.
If X is already compact, ω is an isolated point and the formula needs the convention S_ω = ∅, giving χ_! = χ. This is fine but unstated.
The classes C_∞ and E_X are undefined on the page, so steps (a) and (b) cannot be fully checked.
